items.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009
items.q: So hearing Louis Armstrong on records like that was for me just puzzling to me.

ctx.x: Well I was going to ask, if you’re trying to play and you’re trying to absorb and learn the style of people who were playing almost a hundred years ago, is some of it dependent on what kind of accompaniment you’re getting? And if it’s not there —

I struggled with that. I still struggle with that. I mean there being a disparity. Not as much, I’ve kind of figured it out, but yeah it was really interesting to recognize that there was going to be a disparity, not with just the rhythm section and the accompaniment but even with the other musicians, even the brass players. If I’m in the front line and I got the trumpet player not really playing a whole lot of melody and playing bebop, you know, the counterpoint ends up being a little bit different. It’s not…
